methodology_disclosure: Real Chromium visual and usability checks at the recorded viewports. Speed diagnostics were not requested and do not affect the design verdict.

issues.detail: 3 of 4 sections have no visual moment (no art, media, 3D or type-as-image covering a quarter of the section), e.g. <section#care> "Care, consideredGood care startswith und"; <section#questions> "It's okay to askA few thingson your mind"; <section#appointment> "One small next stepLet's make roomfor yo" at 1440px wide (each section needs one dominant visual drawn from its own content)

2 of 4 sections are built from 1px-ruled boxes or rows (<section#care> "Care, consideredGood care startswith und"; <section#first-visit> "Illustrative room photo · Katarzyna Zygn") at 1440px wide: it reads as a wireframe. Separate surfaces by tone, scale and space; keep rules for real tables

None of 4 sections breaks its frame at 1440px wide (no type set over a picture, no full-bleed picture, nothing crossing a section edge): the page stays flat. Let at least two sections overlap or bleed

Only 0 distinct motion idea(s) found across scroll positions and declared animations (need 6 for a bold page, default): build one scroll- or hand-driven signature set piece from the subject (a pinned stage that changes with scroll counts), or declare <meta name="layoza-motion" content="calm"> if the page is meant to be quiet

No signature set piece found: no pinned stage changes with scroll and no animation is linked to scroll. Build one scroll- or hand-driven scene from the subject (what it does or reveals), or declare <meta name="layoza-motion" content="calm"> if the page is meant to be still

issues.measured: 1800x1350 source for a 629x425 slot (2.9x the pixels needed at 1dppx)
issues.why: The browser downloads and decodes far more pixels than the slot shows, which slows LCP on phones.
issues.fix: Serve srcset/sizes candidates close to the rendered width (x device pixel ratio).
issues.detail: section.wrap.n-index > figure > img: 1800x1350 source for a 629x425 slot (2.9x the pixels needed at 1dppx). Serve srcset/sizes candidates close to the rendered width (x device pixel ratio).

issues.measured: 1800x2700 source for a 590x400 slot (3.0x the pixels needed at 1dppx)
issues.why: The browser downloads and decodes far more pixels than the slot shows, which slows LCP on phones.
issues.fix: Serve srcset/sizes candidates close to the rendered width (x device pixel ratio).
issues.detail: div.wrap.n-first-inner > figure > img: 1800x2700 source for a 590x400 slot (3.0x the pixels needed at 1dppx). Serve srcset/sizes candidates close to the rendered width (x device pixel ratio).

issues.measured: 3 lines, last line 31% of the longest
issues.why: A multi-line heading with one long line and one short line reads lopsided.
issues.fix: Set text-wrap: balance on headings, or adjust the max-width so the lines are even.
issues.detail: div > div.n-copy > h1: 3 lines, last line 31% of the longest. Set text-wrap: balance on headings, or adjust the max-width so the lines are even.

issues.why: A single short word alone on the last line of a heading or paragraph breaks the shape of the block and reads as an accident.
issues.fix: Add text-wrap: pretty to running text, or text-wrap: balance to headings.
issues.detail: section.wrap.n-index > div > p.n-first-note: "pause." alone on line 3 (42px of 408px). Add text-wrap: pretty to running text, or text-wrap: balance to headings.

issues.why: A single short word alone on the last line of a heading or paragraph breaks the shape of the block and reads as an accident.
issues.fix: Add text-wrap: pretty to running text, or text-wrap: balance to headings.
issues.detail: section#care > div.n-section-top > p: "you." alone on line 3 (26px of 296px). Add text-wrap: pretty to running text, or text-wrap: balance to headings.

issues.why: Many unrelated font sizes mean there is no type scale; hierarchy becomes guesswork.
issues.fix: Pick 5-7 sizes from a ratio-based scale and map every text role to one of them.
issues.detail: body.variant-a: 14 distinct text sizes: 9/11/12/13/14/15/16/20/29/47/48/55/60/76px. Pick 5-7 sizes from a ratio-based scale and map every text role to one of them.

issues.why: Skipped heading levels (h2 to h4) break the outline screen-reader users navigate by and usually mean headings were picked for size, not structure.
issues.fix: Use the next level down and size it with CSS.
issues.detail: div.wrap.n-values > article:nth-of-type(1) > h3: h1 then h3. Use the next level down and size it with CSS.

issues.why: The browser's default blue selection and caret are the one place the brand never reached; finished pages theme them.
issues.fix: Set ::selection (and caret-color/accent-color on forms) from the palette tokens.
issues.detail: body.variant-a: no ::selection rule in readable stylesheets. Set ::selection (and caret-color/accent-color on forms) from the palette tokens.

issues.measured: 4 of 4 h2 headings carry an all-caps label above them
issues.why: A small all-caps label sits above most section headings; repeated on every section it stops labelling anything and reads as a template habit.
issues.fix: Keep a label only where it carries information (a category, a date); let most headings stand alone.
issues.detail: div.n-section-top > div > h2: 4 of 4 h2 headings carry an all-caps label above them. Keep a label only where it carries information (a category, a date); let most headings stand alone.

issues.measured: 5 form fields, no :user-invalid / [aria-invalid] / .error style in any stylesheet
issues.why: The form has no styles for invalid or error states, so a rejected field looks identical to a valid one.
issues.fix: Style :user-invalid or [aria-invalid=true] with a colour plus an icon or message, and reserve space so the message does not shift the layout.
issues.detail: form#appointment-form: 5 form fields, no :user-invalid / [aria-invalid] / .error style in any stylesheet. Style :user-invalid or [aria-invalid=true] with a colour plus an icon or message, and reserve space so the message does not shift the layout.

issues.measured: logo left, 4 centred links, 1 button right
issues.why: Wordmark left, four or five centred links and one button right is the default generated navigation; it gives the brand nothing of its own.
issues.fix: Shape the navigation around how this audience moves through the site (fewer links, a search, a booking entry, a different placement).
issues.detail: body.variant-a > header.wrap.n-nav: logo left, 4 centred links, 1 button right. Shape the navigation around how this audience moves through the site (fewer links, a search, a booking entry, a different placement).
